card: Count mined transaction weight instead of local mempool weight when assessing mempool estimator health. Because transactions removed for a block match by txid, differences in witness data between the local mempool and the mined block can skew coverage calculations and report a false healthy status when actual block coverage is below 75%. The change iterates through block transactions in one pass, matching removed entries in block order and accumulating the block's witness weight, accompanied by a unit test and updated RPC documentation.
evidence: PR description: 'If a block confirms a lighter witness variant than the one in our mempool, the estimator counts our heavier variant, so the health check can pass even when the matched transactions make up less than 75% of the mined weight. A heavier mined variant has the opposite effect and understates coverage.'
Test mempool_health_uses_mined_witness_weight verifies that when mined transactions have smaller witnesses than mempool entries, coverage is correctly marked LOW_COVERAGE instead of passing.
problem: Mempool health checks compare the weight of removed mempool transactions to mined block weight, but transactions are matched by txid, which does not commit to witness data. If a block confirms a lighter or heavier witness variant than the mempool variant, counting the local weight skews the health ratio, potentially causing the 75% coverage check to falsely pass or fail.

risk.why: A flaw in mempool health calculation could cause nodes to use inaccurate fee estimates or fail to fall back to block policy estimates.

summary: Calculate mempool fee estimator block coverage using the weight of transactions as mined rather than their weight in the local mempool. When a confirmed transaction matches a mempool entry by txid, its non-witness-dependent match is counted using the block's weight in a single pass over the block.
